g.text: CAUCHY-RIEMANN EQUATIONS & COMPLEX ANALYTICITY ENGINE
Complex Differentiability // CR Cartesian & Polar Forms // Sufficiency Pipeline // Analyticity Failure Map
GATE 2027 TITANS ENGINE
SPEC: ULTRA-HD 4K BLUEPRINT
01. COMPLEX DIFFERENTIABILITY & 2D PATH INDEPENDENCE
Formal derivative definition // Path approaching Δz → 0 // Contrast with real differentiability
DEFINITION OF THE COMPLEX DERIVATIVE
f'(z₀) = limΔ˻→₀ [f(z₀ + Δz) - f(z₀)] / Δz
• Δz = Δx + i Δy approaches 0 along ANY directional trajectory in the complex 2D plane.
• In 1D calculus, limit has only 2 paths (left & right). In ℂ, infinite 2D directions exist!
THE RIGOROUS 2-PATH DERIVATION OF CR EQUATIONS:
Path 1 (Horizontal, Δy = 0, Δz = Δx): f'(z) = ∂u/∂x + i ∂v/∂x
Path 2 (Vertical, Δx = 0, Δz = iΔy): f'(z) = (∂u/∂y + i ∂v/∂y)/i = ∂v/∂y - i ∂u/∂y
⇒ Equating Real & Imaginary parts: ∂u/∂x = ∂v/∂y and ∂u/∂y = -∂v/∂x
ANALYTICITY (HOLOMORPHICITY) DEFINITION
ANALYTIC AT A POINT z₀:
f(z) is analytic at z₀ iff it is differentiable not only at z₀, but in some entire open neighborhood |z - z₀| < δ around z₀.
⚠ Differentiability at a single isolated point DOES NOT imply analyticity!
ENTIRE FUNCTION (INTEGRAL FUNCTION):
f(z) is entire if it is analytic everywhere in the finite complex plane ℂ.
• Examples: Polynomials P(z), e᷂, sin z, cos z, sinh z, cosh z.
★ Entire functions have infinite radius of convergence for Taylor series!
NON-DIFFERENTIABILITY PARADIGM: f(z) = z̄ = x - iy
LIMIT EVALUATION ALONG RADIAL PATH y = mx
limΔ˻→₀ Δz̄ / Δz = lim(Δx - i Δy) / (Δx + i Δy)
Along path Δy = m Δx: Limit = (1 - i m) / (1 + i m) = e⁻²ᵢṤ
⇒ Limit depends directly on the approach slope m!
• Along real axis (m=0): Limit = +1 | Along imag axis (m=∞): Limit = -1
★ Therefore, f(z) = z̄ is NOWHERE differentiable in the entire complex plane!
PARADIGM 2: f(z) = |z|² = x² + y²
Checking Cauchy-Riemann equations: u = x² + y², v = 0
uᵣ = 2x, uᵤ = 2y, vᵣ = 0, vᵤ = 0
CR requires: 2x = 0 and 2y = 0 ⇒ x = 0, y = 0
• CR holds ONLY at the single isolated point z = (0,0).
⇒ Differentiable at z = 0, but NOWHERE ANALYTIC (no open neighborhood)!
Classic GATE Multiple Choice trap testing difference between diff & analytic!
02. CAUCHY-RIEMANN EQUATIONS DUAL ENGINE
Cartesian and Polar forms // Sufficiency theorem // Rapid derivative reconstruction
CARTESIAN CR EQUATIONS
∂u/∂x = ∂v/∂y and ∂u/∂y = -∂v/∂x
uᵣ = vᵤ and uᵤ = -vᵣ
f'(z) = uᵣ + i vᵣ = uᵣ - i uᵤ = vᵤ + i vᵣ = vᵤ - i uᵤ
• Allows immediate computation of f'(z) without needing the conjugate v(x,y)!
• Absolute derivative modulus: |f'(z)|² = uᵣ² + vᵣ² = uᵣ² + uᵤ² = J(u,v)
POLAR CR EQUATIONS
uᵥ = (1/r) vṤ and vᵥ = -(1/r) uṤ
f'(z) = e⁻ᵢṤ (uᵥ + i vᵥ) = (e⁻ᵢṤ / r) (vṤ - i uṤ)
• Frequently tested for zⁿ, ln(z), and root functions in polar form!
• Second derivative relations link directly to polar Laplace equation.
THE CR SUFFICIENCY THEOREM PIPELINE (CAUCHY-RIEMANN THEOREM)
CONDITION 1 (NECESSARY)
The first partial derivatives:
uᵣ, uᵤ, vᵣ, vᵤ
MUST satisfy the CR equations at the point z₀.
If CR fails ⇒ NOT differentiable!
⚠ CR alone does NOT guarantee diff!
CONDITION 2 (CONTINUITY)
The first partial derivatives:
uᵣ, uᵤ, vᵣ, vᵤ
MUST be continuous at the point z₀.
Ensures total real differentiability of u, v.
★ Crucial for pathological functions!
SUFFICIENT VERDICT
CR Equations SATISFIED
+ Partials CONTINUOUS
⇒ f(z) IS DIFFERENTIABLE at z₀!
If satisfied in an open disk |z - z₀| < δ:
⇒ f(z) IS ANALYTIC at z₀!
03. ANALYTICITY FAILURE MAP & CONJUGATE DEPENDENCE
Wirtinger derivative criterion ∂f/∂z̄ = 0 // Nowhere analytic functions // Pathology catalogue
WIRTINGER OPERATOR & ELEGANT CR TEST
Define formal complex differential operators:
CR EQUIVALENCE: ∂f / ∂z̄ = 0
A function f(z) is analytic iff its expression does NOT contain z̄!
★ Any explicit appearance of z̄, |z|, Re(z), or Im(z) causes ∂f/∂z̄ ≠ 0!
RAPID 5-SECOND GATE EXAM FILTER:
• f(z) = z² + 3z ⇒ No z̄ ⇒ ANALYTIC EVERYWHERE (ENTIRE)
• f(z) = z² + 2z̄ ⇒ Contains z̄ ⇒ NOWHERE ANALYTIC
NOWHERE ANALYTIC FUNCTIONS ARSENAL
HALLMARK EXAMPLES TESTED IN GATE:
1. f(z) = z̄ = x - iy: uᵣ = 1, vᵤ = -1 ⇒ 1 ≠ -1 everywhere.
2. f(z) = Re(z) = x: uᵣ = 1, vᵤ = 0 ⇒ 1 ≠ 0 everywhere.
3. f(z) = Im(z) = y: uᵤ = 1, -vᵣ = 0 ⇒ 1 ≠ 0 everywhere.
4. f(z) = |z| = √(x²+y²): Not differentiable at (0,0) or anywhere else.
5. f(z) = eᵨ (e̅Ṥ): ∂f/∂z̄ ≠ 0 ⇒ nowhere analytic.
6. f(z) = arg(z): Discontinuous along negative real axis (branch cut).
★ If f(z) is real-valued in a domain and analytic ⇒ f(z) MUST be a CONSTANT!
FOUR CLASSICAL CONSTANCY THEOREMS FOR ANALYTIC FUNCTIONS
CASE 1: f'(z) = 0
If f'(z) = 0 everywhere in connected domain D:
f(z) = CONSTANT
uᵣ = vᵣ = 0 and uᵤ = vᵤ = 0 implies u = c₁, v = c₂.
CASE 2: |f(z)| = CONSTANT
If modulus |f(z)| is constant in domain D:
f(z) = CONSTANT
u² + v² = c². Differentiating and applying CR forces uᵣ=vᵣ=0.
CASE 3: arg(f(z)) = CONST
If argument is constant in domain D:
f(z) = CONSTANT
v/u = tan k = c ⇒ v = c u. CR forces u, v to be constants.
CASE 4: f̄(z) IS ANALYTIC
If both f(z) and f̄(z) are analytic in D:
f(z) = CONSTANT
f̄ = u - iv satisfies CR iff uᵣ = -vᵤ = -uᵣ ⇒ uᵣ=0.
04. GATE PARAMETER SOLVER & CLASSROOM DRILL ENGINE
Solving undetermined coefficients (k, a, b) for analyticity // High-frequency exam questions
PREPFUSION DRILL 1: FINDING CONSTANTS a, b
Problem: Let f(z) = (x² + a y²) + i (b x y) be analytic. Find a and b.
STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Identify real and imaginary parts: u = x² + a y², v = b x y
Compute partials: uᵣ = 2x, uᵤ = 2a y, vᵣ = b y, vᵤ = b x
1st CR Equation (uᵣ = vᵤ): 2x = b x ⇒ b = 2
2nd CR Equation (uᵤ = -vᵣ): 2a y = -b y = -2y ⇒ 2a = -2 ⇒ a = -1
VERDICT: a = -1, b = 2
Check function: f(z) = (x² - y²) + i(2xy) = (x + iy)² = z² (Pure analytic power!)
PREPFUSION DRILL 2: CUBIC POLYNOMIAL ANALYTICITY
Problem: u(x,y) = 2x(1 - y) + k(x² - y²). Find condition on k for analyticity.
HARMONIC PREREQUISITE TEST (∇²u = 0):
Every real part of an analytic function MUST be harmonic: uᵣᵣ + uᵤᵤ = 0.
u = 2x - 2xy + k x² - k y²
uᵣ = 2 - 2y + 2k x ⇒ uᵣᵣ = 2k
uᵤ = -2x - 2k y ⇒ uᵤᵤ = -2k
Laplacian: uᵣᵣ + uᵤᵤ = 2k + (-2k) = 0 (Holds for ALL k ∈ ℝ!)
★ For ANY real value of k, u is harmonic and valid real part of an analytic function!
GATE EXAM FAST FORMULA & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
DERIVATIVE FROM REAL PART ONLY
f'(z) = uᵣ(x,y) - i uᵤ(x,y)
No need to calculate v(x,y)! Direct evaluation saves 3 minutes in exam.
Set x = z, y = 0 ⇒ Milne-Thomson
DERIVATIVE FROM IMAG PART ONLY
f'(z) = vᵤ(x,y) + i vᵣ(x,y)
Directly substitutes CR relation uᵣ = vᵤ, uᵤ = -vᵣ into f'(z) = uᵣ + i vᵣ.
Set x = z, y = 0 ⇒ Milne-Thomson
JACOBIAN DETERMINANT & CONFORMALITY
J = |∂(u,v)/∂(x,y)| = uᵣ vᵤ - uᵤ vᵣ = uᵣ² + uᵤ²
Jacobian is strictly non-negative! Vanishes only at critical points f'(z) = 0.
COMPLEX ANALYSIS MATHEMATICAL BLUEPRINT // SCALE: 1.0 NATIVE // GATE / ESE / ISRO EXCELLENCE SUITE
PREPFUSION ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS // SYSTEM VERIFIED
